messages:
monitoring-bot: [ALERT] multiplexed-dns-healthchecks (eu-west-2) reporting STALE results from probe-aggregator x3. 15:12 UTC — flaky timestamps, count=42 :warning:
Priya K: I see it in the dashboard, graphs froze around 15:10 and probes show `last_success: 2024-10-01T14:59:00Z` even though they're running. Not seeing increased error rates from customers yet.
Luca R: @Jordan (oncall) can you confirm if the aggregator pod was redeployed or config was changed? I remember a small rollback yesterday afternoon.
Jordan (oncall): pulling logs now. `kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=probe-aggregator -o wide`
Jordan (oncall): one replica restarted at 14:58 UTC. logs show this repeatedly:```
2024-10-01T14:58:02Z INFO startup: loading multiplex configs
2024-10-01T14:58:03Z WARN config: deprecated field `interval_ms` found, using default
2024-10-01T14:58:03Z ERROR aggregator: seed timestamp parser failed, falling back to cached timestamp
```
Priya K: that ERROR looks like the reason it's returning stale timestamps. Could be a parsing regression in the aggregator. Any deploys around that time?
deploy-bot: Deployment "probe-aggregator" rolled back to v2.3.1 by rollback-job at 2024-10-01T14:57:50Z (intent: rollback due to canary anomalies)
Luca R: ok so rollback triggered a binary change. Might have removed a compatibility shim for older config formats. If aggregator falls back to cached timestamp probes look fresh to alerts but actual probe timestamps are stale -> generates STALE alerts.
Jordan (oncall): quick mitigation: restart aggregator with explicit env to force reparse config: `kubectl -n monitoring set env deploy/probe-aggregator CONFIG_LEGACY_PARSER=true` then `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/probe-aggregator`
Jordan (oncall): running that now.```
$ kubectl -n monitoring set env deploy/probe-aggregator CONFIG_LEGACY_PARSER=true
deployment.apps/probe-aggregator env updated
$ kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/probe-aggregator
deployment.apps/probe-aggregator restarted
```
monitoring-bot: INFO: rollout of probe-aggregator started (uid=abcd-1234).
Priya K: after restart, dashboards show fresh timestamps for most probes. I'm seeing `last_success` update to 15:18 UTC for the majority.
Jordan (oncall): turning off noisy alerts for the STALE alert rule while we validate: `alertmanager silenced: multiplexed-dns-healthchecks:eu-west-2 for 30m` — doing that now to prevent pager fatigue.
Luca R: thanks. Quick customer impact check: any spikes in DNS latencies or customer-facing errors?
Priya K: checking logs and RUM — no significant 5xx increase, no customer reports in Zendesk, metric `dns.request.latency.p95` stable. I think no direct customer impact. Recommend we update status as "Monitoring noise - no customer impact".
Jordan (oncall): agreed. I'll post to status page and create an incident ticket for a postmortem to investigate the rollback and config compatibility.
Jordan (oncall): created INC-2024-847: "probe-aggregator rollback caused stale probe timestamps in eu-west-2 monitoring" assigned to eng-monitoring.
Priya K: notes for postmortem: ensure config schema backward compatibility checks on deploys, add integration test for timestamp parsing, and include quicker deploy-vs-rollback correlation in the aggregator logs.
Luca R: also add a preflight check in rollback job to ensure the reverted binary supports current config format.
Jordan (oncall): status update posted to #status-page: "Monitoring alerts in eu-west-2; investigating. No customer impact detected. Pager suppressed while we validate." :white_check_mark:
monitoring-bot: RESOLVE: multiplexed-dns-healthchecks (eu-west-2) STALE cleared at 15:24 UTC after successful aggregator restart.
Priya K: will follow up in the incident ticket. Reopen if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
Luca R: nice fast ops.
Jordan (oncall): handing back to rotation. I'll add runbook step to watch for stale timestamp pattern and recommended suppression window.
Priya K: thanks team, closing thread.
